metric.name: binder_wait_ms
metric.sql_used:
INCLUDE PERFETTO MODULE android.binder;
INCLUDE PERFETTO MODULE android.frames.timeline;
WITH
  window_frames AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT f.upid, f.ui_thread_utid, a.id, a.dur, a.jank_type
    FROM android_frames_layers AS f
    JOIN actual_frame_timeline_slice AS a ON a.id = f.actual_frame_timeline_id
    WHERE f.layer_name NOT GLOB '*SurfaceView*' AND a.dur > 0
  ),
  app AS (
    SELECT upid FROM window_frames GROUP BY upid ORDER BY count(*) DESC, upid LIMIT 1
  ),
  frames AS (
    SELECT * FROM window_frames WHERE upid = (SELECT upid FROM app)
  )
SELECT
  CASE
    WHEN NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM frames)
      OR NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM android_binder_txns) THEN NULL
    ELSE coalesce((
      SELECT sum(client_dur) FROM android_binder_txns
      WHERE is_sync AND client_dur > 0
        AND client_utid IN (SELECT ui_thread_utid FROM frames)
    ), 0) / 1e6
  END AS value

claims.text: Synchronous binder wait on the app's UI thread increased from 287.81833 ms in the baseline to 348.319381 ms in the current trace, a delta of 60.501051 ms.

claims.text: The increased UI-thread binder wait is concentrated in synchronous calls to SurfaceFlinger; the grouped trace query reports 371 calls and 277.81742 ms in the baseline, versus 400 calls and 348.318318 ms in the current trace.

The range includes a FeedScreen change that rewrites player acquisition using takeIf, but the trace evidence only identifies SurfaceFlinger binder activity and does not connect that activity to this commit.

caveats: Each side is represented by a single capture, so the binder delta may be run-to-run variance.
The captures ran on an Android emulator (sdk_gphone64_arm64, SDK 36), which can add variability to SurfaceFlinger and binder timing.
The current build was a non-debuggable benchmark build; baseline build metadata was not available.
